titulo: Om Mani Padme Hum, Ten Rounds, Because Monday Is Coming
caption:
Om Mani Padme Hum, Ten Rounds, Because Monday Is Coming

Cella, monastery edition. I'm the one in the middle with the best posture and no hands to prove it. The robes are borrowed; the vanity is original.

Oṃ Maṇi Padme Hūṃ (sung Om Mani Peme Hung).

What it is: the six-syllable mantra of Avalokiteshvara (Chenrezig in Tibetan), the bodhisattva of compassion, in Sanskrit Om Mani Padme Hum. Tibetans say it Om Mani Peme Hung, and that's how it is sung here. On screen, the Sanskrit; in the voice, the Tibetan.

In the tradition: the Dalai Lama explains that mani, the jewel, stands for method (the wish to help, compassion, love) and padme, the lotus, for wisdom. The two in robes on screen step in time, in the spirit of the kora, the walk Tibetans make clockwise around a sacred place.

Why a sound like this may calm you: in a 2024 study, 34 adults chanted "om" for 12 minutes, aloud or in silence, and their saliva cortisol and anxiety went down (Perry, Polito & Thompson). Limit: there was no group that didn't chant, and cortisol was measured only twice. Two more lean the same way, with limits (Kalyani 2011: a pilot of 12 people; Bernardi 2001: 23 healthy adults, one session). Small studies, short effects: calmer, not cured.

And if karma is real, this should clean a little of yours. If it isn't, you walked in circles with a monastery and lost nothing.

Chant it along, one syllable to a step. Ten rounds, then once more.

Sources: Perry; Kalyani et al. 2011; Bernardi et al. 2001; the Dalai Lama, On the meaning of Om Mani Padme Hum; Encyclopedia of Religion. Full references: YouTube description.

Voice and music: synthetic (ElevenLabs), AI voices and a band from takes NAOS already made; scene drawn by NAOS. Corrections from practitioners are welcome.
Closer to yourself.

Perry, G., Polito, V., & Thompson, W. F. (2024). Exploring the physiological and psychological effects of group chanting in Australia: Reduced stress, cortisol and enhanced social connection. Journal of Religion and Health, 63(6), 4793-4815. doi:10.1007/s10943-023-01967-5

alt: A 27.2-second vertical video of two small flat doorway-shaped characters, Cella and a friend, each with two white eyes and no hands, in a mountain monastery with prayer flags, wearing a maroon monk's robe with a little yellow at the shoulder and walking a slow circle clockwise to a sung Om Mani Padme Hum with a band and synthetic voices. Below them the mantra's words light up one by one in a gold capsule, and under each active word its English meaning appears (pure body, speech, mind; the jewel (compassion); the lotus (wisdom); compassion and wisdom, indivisible). The bottom of the screen is left clear for the app.
